room_name: Le service population · The registration office
hook: "ah-ZHAHNS": a smiling travel-AGENCY lady zooms a toy airplane across a big desk map for a young couple planning their trip: an AGENCY arranges things for you: AGENCY
note: Une agence is an agency or office (une agence de voyages = travel agency; une agence immobilière = real-estate agency; une agence bancaire = bank branch). The person is un agent, une agente. Not to be confused with l'agenda (a diary or planner).

room_name: Le service population · The registration office
hook: "ee-dahn-tee-TAY": at the counter a puzzled clerk looks from one twin brother to the other: two IDENTICAL faces, so whose IDENTITY is whose?: IDENTITY
note: L'identité is identity (une carte d'identité = an ID card; une pièce d'identité = any photo ID; un contrôle d'identité = an ID check). Une erreur d'identité is mistaken identity. Like English, it can also mean sameness (l'identité de deux choses).

room_name: Le service population · The registration office
hook: "ahd-mee-nees-trah-TEEF": a frazzled clerk balances a teetering ADMINISTRATIVE tower of paper forms on her desk: ADMINISTRATIVE
note: Administratif means administrative (les démarches administratives = official paperwork; un centre administratif = government offices). Masc. administratif, fem. administrative. Le personnel administratif is the office staff; la paperasse administrative is red tape.

room_name: Le service population · The registration office
change: added (Monsieur Verbe mime, red beret; conjugation added); vocab room ST_communication_seg008 -> R_admin_01
hook: "kohn-feer-MAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) CONFIRMS the appointment with a big FIRM handshake across the counter, nodding hard: yes, it's settled!: CONFIRM (a FIRM handshake)
note: Confirmer means to confirm (confirmer un rendez-vous, une réservation) and, of a court, to uphold a decision (confirmer un jugement). Se confirmer is to be confirmed (La nouvelle se confirme). The opposite is démentir or infirmer (to deny, to overturn).

room_name: Le service population · The registration office
change: added (Monsieur Verbe mime, red beret; conjugation added); vocab room ST_communication_seg012 -> R_admin_01
hook: "CONVOY-KAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) beckons a little CONVOY of children on ride-on toy trucks to come in: he SUMMONS them (kohn-voh-KAY): CONVOY-KAY
note: Convoquer means to summon or call someone in officially (être convoqué à la mairie, au commissariat, à un entretien) and to convene a meeting (convoquer une assemblée). Une convocation is the official letter calling you in. It never means to convoy; that is escorter or convoyer.

room_name: Le service population · The registration office
hook: "ah-rohn-dee-suh-MAHN": on the wall, a big map of Paris whose districts spiral out like a snail shell, and a real garden snail crawls along the spiral of ARRONDISSEMENTS: SNAIL MAP
note: Un arrondissement is a district of a big city: Paris, Lyon and Marseille are divided into numbered arrondissements (j'habite dans le 11e). It is also a subdivision of a French département. Arrondir means to round off, and l'arrondissement is also the rounding of a number.

room_name: Le service population · The registration office
hook: "day-pahr-tuh-MAHN": a boy presses the last puzzle piece into a big jigsaw map of France: each piece is one DÉPARTEMENT: DEPARTMENT jigsaw
note: Un département is one of France's 101 administrative areas (le département du Rhône); each has a number used in postcodes. It also means a department of a company, store or university (le département des ventes; un département de français). A department store is un grand magasin, not un département.

room_name: Le service population · The registration office
hook: "FISHER-YAY": a FISHERman in waders casts his rod into an open drawer of the filing cabinet, hooks a FILE folder and cheers 'YAY!': FISHER-YAY
note: Un fichier is a file: a computer file (enregistrer un fichier) or a card index, a register of records (le fichier des clients). A paper folder is un dossier or une chemise. Ficher (no i) means to put on file or, informally, to do or to throw (Je m'en fiche = I don't care).

room_name: Le service population · The registration office
hook: "sehr-tee-fee-KAH": a proud new mom with a baby in a sling holds the BIRTH CERTIFICATE with a gold seal and a pink ribbon: BIRTH CERTIFICATE
note: Un certificat is a certificate or official proof (un certificat de naissance = birth certificate; un certificat médical = doctor's note). It can also be a diploma or credential. Un certificat de scolarité proves you are enrolled at a school.

room_name: Le service population · The registration office
hook: "day-KREH": a town crier in a tricorn hat unrolls a long scroll and announces the mayor's DECREE to the queue: DECREE
note: Un décret is a decree, an order issued by the government or the President (publier un décret); un décret d'application puts a law into effect. Décréter means to decree or, loosely, to declare something by decision (Il a décrété que c'était fini).

room_name: Le parlement des jeunes · The youth parliament
hook: "day-moh-krah-SEE": a teacher points to a big poster of an ancient Greek temple with columns: Athens, the birthplace of DEMOCRACY: DEMOCRACY (Greek temple)
note: La démocratie is democracy (vivre en démocratie). Une démocratie is also a democratic country. Its opposites are la dictature (dictatorship) and la tyrannie. Un démocrate is a democrat, a supporter of democracy (not a party label in France).

room_name: Le parlement des jeunes · The youth parliament
hook: "ay-lehk-SYOHN": on election night a teen teller sorts paper ballots into two neat piles on a small table: the ELECTION count: ELECTION count
note: Une élection is an election (les élections municipales = local elections; se présenter aux élections = to run). Une élection can also be the choice of one person by vote (son élection à la présidence). The verb is élire; an elector is un électeur.

room_name: Le parlement des jeunes · The youth parliament
hook: "oh-poh-zee-SYOHN": on the far bench, the OPPOSITION all fold their arms and shake their heads at the proposal: OPPOSITION
note: L'opposition is opposition: the parties against the government (les partis d'opposition; le chef de l'opposition) and any resistance (faire opposition à). Faire opposition à un chèque is to stop a check. Par opposition à means as opposed to.

room_name: Le parlement des jeunes · The youth parliament
hook: "kohns-tee-tew-SYOHN": two pupils solemnly carry an enormous leather-bound book, the CONSTITUTION, on a red velvet cushion: CONSTITUTION
note: La constitution is a country's constitution (la Constitution de 1958) and also a person's build or health (une solide constitution = a strong constitution) or how something is made up (la constitution d'une équipe = the forming of a team).

room_name: Le parlement des jeunes · The youth parliament
hook: "pray-zee-dahn-SYEHL": a girl climbs proudly into the tall carved PRESIDENTIAL chair at the raised desk while two classmates pull it out for her: PRESIDENTIAL chair
note: Présidentiel (présidentielle) means presidential (le fauteuil présidentiel; l'élection présidentielle). La présidentielle on its own is the presidential election. It also fits any chair of a club or meeting: la table présidentielle is the head table. The noun is la présidence, the presidency.

room_name: Le parlement des jeunes · The youth parliament
hook: "pahr-luh-MAHN": on the back wall a big painting of a domed PARLIAMENT building, and a girl points at it explaining where laws are made: PARLIAMENT painting
note: Le parlement is a parliament; in France le Parlement is the Assemblée nationale plus the Sénat. Un parlementaire is a member of parliament. Before 1789 a parlement was a royal law court. Parler (to speak) is the root: a parliament is where people talk things out.

room_name: Le parlement des jeunes · The youth parliament
hook: "VOT": on the right benches the members all VOTE by holding up green voting cards high: VOTE cards
note: Le vote is a vote or the voting (le vote à main levée = a show of hands; le droit de vote = the right to vote). Un vote blanc is a blank ballot. The verb is voter; a voter is un électeur, not un voteur.

room_name: Le parlement des jeunes · The youth parliament
hook: "pahr-TEE (PARTY)": the members of one PARTY all wear matching orange rosettes and wave matching orange balloons, celebrating their win: PARTY
note: Un parti is a political party (le parti socialiste; adhérer à un parti). Careful: a party you go to is une fête or une soirée, not un parti. Prendre parti means to take sides; un beau parti is a good match for marriage.

room_name: Le parlement des jeunes · The youth parliament
hook: "ruh-pray-zahn-TAHN": classmates push a shy boy forward holding their class teddy-bear mascot: he is their REPRESENTATIVE: REPRESENTATIVE
note: Un représentant, une représentante is a representative or delegate (les représentants du personnel), and also a sales representative (un représentant de commerce). Un représentant du peuple is an elected member of parliament.

room_name: Le parlement des jeunes · The youth parliament
hook: "day-moh-krah-TEEK": pupils each drop a bead into one of two big glass jars to choose the class pet by DEMOCRATIC vote: DEMOCRATIC jars
note: Démocratique means democratic (un pays démocratique; une décision démocratique). The opposite is antidémocratique or autoritaire. It describes a system or decision, not a party: the U.S. Democratic Party is le Parti démocrate.

room_name: Le parlement des jeunes · The youth parliament
hook: "goo-vehr-nuh-mahn-TAHL": a courier in a dark suit sets down a red leather GOVERNMENTAL dispatch box tied with a blue, white and red ribbon: GOVERNMENTAL red box
note: Gouvernemental means governmental, of the government (une décision gouvernementale; une source gouvernementale). An ONG (organisation non gouvernementale) is an NGO. Le gouvernement is the government; gouverner is to govern or to steer a boat.

room_name: Le parlement des jeunes · The youth parliament
change: added (Monsieur Verbe mime, red beret; conjugation added); vocab room ST_rule_seg006 -> R_politics_03
hook: "ah-proo-VAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) APPROVES loudly: he applauds and nods with a big smile at the new president: APPROVE (applause)
note: Approuver means to approve of, to agree with (J'approuve ton choix) and to approve officially, ratify (approuver un budget). Lu et approuvé = read and approved, written above a signature. The opposite is désapprouver.

room_name: La salle des débats · The debate room
hook: "CLAIRE-uh-MAHN": CLAIRE holds a glass of crystal-CLEAR water up to the lamp so everyone sees CLEARLY there is nothing hidden in it: CLAIRE + CLEAR
note: Clairement means clearly: plainly visible or understandable (expliquer clairement) and obviously, without doubt (Il a clairement tort). Its opposite is vaguement or confusément. Claire is also a girl's name meaning bright, clear.

room_name: La salle des débats · The debate room
hook: "FRANK-uh-MAHN": a blunt man waves a hot dog, a FRANK, as he speaks FRANKLY at the microphone: no beating about the bush: FRANK-ly (a frank)
note: Franchement means frankly, honestly (Franchement, je n'aime pas) and also really, downright (C'est franchement nul = it's downright bad). It can mean decisively, without hesitating (y aller franchement = go for it). As an exclamation, Franchement ! shows annoyance: Honestly!

room_name: La salle des débats · The debate room
hook: "RAY-EL-uh-MAHN": a boy pinches his own arm, wide-eyed, as the mayor hands him the microphone: is this REALLY happening?: REAL-ly (pinch)
note: Réellement means really, actually, genuinely (Il est réellement malade = he is genuinely ill). Réel means real; la réalité is reality. It stresses fact, not intensity: 'really big' is more often vraiment grand. Pas réellement = not really.

room_name: La salle des débats · The debate room
hook: "say-ryeuh-zuh-MAHN": a lady raises her eyebrows at a man who claims his dog can speak, while the dog wears headphones: SERIOUSLY?: SERIOUSLY?
note: Sérieusement means seriously: in earnest (travailler sérieusement) and gravely (sérieusement blessé = seriously injured). Alone, Sérieusement ? means Seriously? Are you kidding? Sérieux is serious; prendre au sérieux is to take seriously.

room_name: La salle des débats · The debate room
hook: "ay-sahn-syeh-luh-MAHN": a perfumer holds up a tiny bottle of rose ESSENCE: just one drop, ESSENTIALLY the whole rose garden: ESSENTIAL (essence)
note: Essentiellement means essentially, mainly, above all (Il s'agit essentiellement d'argent = it's mainly about money). L'essentiel is the main thing (C'est l'essentiel). Note l'essence is also gasoline in France, as well as an essence or extract.

room_name: La salle des débats · The debate room
hook: "oh-neh-tuh-MAHN": a boy HONESTLY hands back a fat wallet he found under a chair to its delighted old owner: HONEST boy
note: Honnêtement means honestly, fairly (gagner sa vie honnêtement) and, at the start of a sentence, frankly (Honnêtement, je ne sais pas). It can also mean decently, reasonably well (C'est honnêtement payé). The opposite is malhonnêtement.

room_name: La salle des débats · The debate room
hook: "lee-tay-rah-luh-MAHN": a man wears enormous fake ears: he is LITERALLY all ears for the debate: LITERALLY all ears
note: Littéralement means literally: word for word (traduire littéralement) and, informally, as an intensifier (Je suis littéralement épuisé = I'm literally exhausted). Au sens littéral = in the literal sense; the opposite is au sens figuré (figuratively).

room_name: La salle des débats · The debate room
hook: "oh-fee-syeh-luh-MAHN": the debate OFFICIAL in a black blazer blows a silver whistle with his arm raised: the debate OFFICIALLY begins: OFFICIAL whistle
note: Officiellement means officially: formally, by the authorities (C'est officiellement fermé) and, sometimes, on paper as opposed to really (Officiellement, il est malade = supposedly he is ill). Officieusement means unofficially, off the record.

room_name: La salle des débats · The debate room
hook: "pew-ruh-MAHN": a girl cradles a PURE-white dove with not one gray feather: PURELY white: PURE white dove
note: Purement means purely, solely (purement et simplement = purely and simply; une question purement technique). Pur means pure (l'eau pure; le pur hasard = pure chance). L'impureté is impurity.

room_name: La salle des débats · The debate room
change: added (Monsieur Verbe mime, red beret; conjugation added); vocab room ST_communication_seg014 -> R_adv_logic_03
hook: "pehr-swah-DAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) pleads with clasped hands and PERSUADES a grumpy old man to sign the petition: the man starts to smile and unfold his arms: PERSUADE
note: Persuader means to persuade or convince (persuader quelqu'un de faire quelque chose). Être persuadé que = to be convinced that. La persuasion is persuasion. The opposite is dissuader (to dissuade, talk out of).

room_name: La salle des débats · The debate room
change: added (Monsieur Verbe mime, gold beret; conjugation added); vocab room ST_communication_seg021 -> R_adv_logic_03
hook: "CONTRA-DEER": a DEER nods yes, yes, yes, and MONSIEUR VERBE (gold beret) CONTRADICTS it, shaking his head and wagging a finger: no, no, no!: CONTRA-DEER
note: Contredire means to contradict (contredire ses parents). It conjugates like dire except vous contredisez (not contredites). Se contredire is to contradict oneself. Une contradiction is a contradiction; l'esprit de contradiction is contrariness.

room_name: La commission d'urbanisme · The planning committee
hook: "ruh-FOOS": a grinning delivery man pushes a FOOSball table at a stern white-haired grandpa, who holds up both palms and turns his head away: REFUSAL
note: Un refus is a refusal (essuyer un refus = meet with a refusal; un refus de permis = a permit denied). Ce n'est pas de refus! means I won't say no! (yes please). The verb is refuser; the opposite is une acceptation or un accord.

room_name: La commission d'urbanisme · The planning committee
change: added (Monsieur Verbe mime, red beret; conjugation added); vocab room ST_communication_seg022 -> R_adv_logic_02
hook: "ray-tor-KAY": a man scoffs at the plans, and MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) RETORTS at once, one finger up, snapping back a quick reply: RETORT
note: Rétorquer means to retort, to reply sharply or quickly (rétorquer que...). It also means to turn an argument back on someone. A synonym is répliquer; une réplique is a retort or a line in a play.

room_name: La commission d'urbanisme · The planning committee
hook: "kohn-treh-ruh-MAHN": two brothers carry one model house and pull it in CONTRARY, opposite directions: CONTRARY
note: Contrairement à means unlike, contrary to (Contrairement à son frère, il est calme). Le contraire is the opposite (au contraire = on the contrary). Contraire is the adjective (des avis contraires = opposing views).

room_name: La commission d'urbanisme · The planning committee
hook: "vah-guh-MAHN": a man squints at a foggy, blurry architect's drawing and can only VAGUELY make out a house: VAGUE fog
note: Vaguement means vaguely, dimly (Je m'en souviens vaguement) or a little, slightly (vaguement inquiet = a bit worried). Careful: une vague is a wave (in the sea, or a wave of heat or of people), but vague as an adjective means vague.

room_name: La commission d'urbanisme · The planning committee
hook: "koh-rehk-tuh-MAHN": a woman sets a spirit level on a model's roof and smiles: the bubble sits dead center, built CORRECTLY: CORRECTLY (spirit level)
note: Correctement means correctly, properly (remplir correctement un formulaire) and decently, acceptably (être payé correctement = paid reasonably). Incorrectement means incorrectly. Correct also means polite, well-behaved (Sois correct avec lui).

room_name: La commission d'urbanisme · The planning committee
hook: "kew-ryeuh-zuh-MAHN": a little girl presses her nose CURIOUSLY to a tiny window of a model house to see inside: CURIOUS
note: Curieusement means curiously in both senses: with curiosity (regarder curieusement) and strangely, oddly (Curieusement, personne n'est venu = oddly, nobody came). Curieux can also mean nosy. Bizarrement is a synonym for oddly.

room_name: La commission d'urbanisme · The planning committee
hook: "DOH-RAY-NAH-VAN": a woman pushes a toy ice-cream VAN across the model village and sings 'DOH, RAY, NAH!': FROM NOW ON, the van comes every day: DOH-RAY-NAH-VAN
note: Dorénavant means from now on, henceforth (Dorénavant, la réunion aura lieu le lundi). It always points to the future; for 'from then on' in the past use désormais or dès lors. Synonyms: désormais, à l'avenir.

room_name: La commission d'urbanisme · The planning committee
hook: "day-fee-nee-tee-vuh-MAHN": a man hammers a model house firmly down onto its base: it is staying there for good, DEFINITIVELY: DEFINITIVELY
note: Définitivement is a false friend: it means for good, permanently (Il est parti définitivement = he left for good), not 'definitely'. For 'definitely' say certainement, sans aucun doute or vraiment. Définitif means final (une réponse définitive).

room_name: La commission d'urbanisme · The planning committee
hook: "NAY-ON-MOAN": a pony loaded with rolled plans says 'NAY!' and MOANS at the weight, but NEVERTHELESS keeps on pulling: NAY-ON-MOAN
note: Néanmoins means nevertheless, nonetheless (C'est cher, néanmoins c'est utile). It is a little formal; in speech people say pourtant or quand même. Synonyms: cependant, toutefois.

room_name: La commission d'urbanisme · The planning committee
hook: "nay-say-seh-ruh-MAHN": a builder steps up to the models and NECESSARILY puts on his yellow hard hat first: no hat, no entry: NECESSARILY hard hat
note: Nécessairement means necessarily, inevitably (Ça finira nécessairement mal). Pas nécessairement = not necessarily. It can also mean as a logical consequence. Nécessaire is necessary; le nécessaire is what is needed (faire le nécessaire = do what's needed).

room_name: La commission d'urbanisme · The planning committee
hook: "streek-tuh-MAHN": a STRICT inspector measures a model fence's height with a yellow tape measure, frowning: STRICTLY by the rules: STRICTLY
note: Strictement means strictly (strictement interdit = strictly forbidden) and, before an adjective, absolutely, utterly (strictement identique; strictement rien = nothing at all). Strict means strict or severe.

room_name: La maison des associations · The clubs' hall
hook: "rehs-treek-SYOHN": at the climbing wall a height-RESTRICTION bar stops a tall teen: he has to duck under it, grinning: RESTRICTION bar
note: Une restriction is a restriction, a limit (des restrictions d'eau = water restrictions; sans restriction = without reservation). Faire des restrictions is also to express reservations. Restreindre is to restrict; restreint means limited.

room_name: La maison des associations · The clubs' hall
hook: "PAIR-ee-TAY": the dance club dances in PAIRS: each pair one woman and one man, exactly equal numbers: PARITY: PAIR-ITY
note: La parité is parity, equality (la parité hommes-femmes = gender parity in elections or pay). In finance it is the parity of two currencies. Un nombre pair is an even number; parité also means evenness.

room_name: La maison des associations · The clubs' hall
hook: "soh-syah-bee-lee-TAY": a very SOCIABLE lady pours coffee from the urn and chats merrily to a whole laughing crowd at once: SOCIABLE
note: La sociabilité is sociability, how much someone enjoys company. Sociable means sociable, friendly; the opposite is insociable or sauvage (shy, unsociable). Les sociabilités in sociology are networks of social life.

room_name: La maison des associations · The clubs' hall
hook: "ay-mahn-see-pah-SYOHN": a girl rides off proudly on her bike while her dad holds up the training wheels he just took off: free at last: EMANCIPATION
note: L'émancipation is emancipation: freeing oneself from control (l'émancipation des femmes) and, legally, a minor gaining adult rights. S'émanciper is to become independent, to break free. Émancipé means emancipated, free-thinking.

room_name: La maison des associations · The clubs' hall
hook: "frah-tehr-nee-TAY": one brother carries his little brother piggyback across the hall: brotherhood, FRATERNITY: FRATERNITY
note: La fraternité is brotherhood, fellowship among people; it is the third word of the French motto Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité. It is not a U.S. college fraternity (une confrérie d'étudiants). Fraternel means brotherly.

room_name: La maison des associations · The clubs' hall
hook: "see-twah-yeh-nuh-TAY": a new citizen with her hand on her heart takes the CITIZENSHIP oath, tears of joy in her eyes, her family clapping: CITIZENSHIP
note: La citoyenneté is citizenship (obtenir la citoyenneté française; acquérir la nationalité is the legal term) and also active, responsible citizenship (l'éducation à la citoyenneté). Un citoyen, une citoyenne is a citizen.

room_name: La maison des associations · The clubs' hall
hook: "ah-noh-nee-MAH": a donor in a hooded coat and dark glasses slips an envelope into the club's donation box and tiptoes away, keeping his ANONYMITY: ANONYMOUS donor
note: L'anonymat is anonymity (garder l'anonymat = to stay anonymous; sous couvert d'anonymat = on condition of anonymity). Anonyme means anonymous; une lettre anonyme is an anonymous letter.

room_name: La maison des associations · The clubs' hall
hook: "ah-sahn-tee-MAHN": a grandpa nods his ASSENT: yes, his grandson may join the chess club: ASSENT nod
note: L'assentiment is assent, agreement, consent (donner son assentiment; d'un commun assentiment = by common consent). It is formal; in everyday speech people say l'accord or le consentement. Assentir is rare.

room_name: La maison des associations · The clubs' hall
hook: "lee-bay-rah-LEEZM": a smiling grocer lifts the barrier of his market stall wide open: FREE trade for all, LIBERALISM: LIBERAL free trade
note: Le libéralisme in France usually means economic liberalism, belief in free markets and limited state control (le libéralisme économique). It is close to what Americans call free-market conservatism, not U.S. 'liberal' politics (which is de gauche or progressiste).

room_name: La maison des associations · The clubs' hall
hook: "see-VEEK": a teen volunteer does her CIVIC duty, sweeping up after the fair with a big broom: CIVIC duty
note: Civique means civic (le devoir civique = civic duty; le sens civique = public spirit). L'instruction civique is civics class. Le service civique is a French voluntary national service for young people.

room_name: La maison des associations · The clubs' hall
hook: "koh-mew-NAHL": the teacher from the COMMUNAL school leads a line of small pupils holding hands past the club tables: COMMUNAL school
note: Communal means belonging to the commune, municipal (l'école communale = the village primary school; la salle communale = the village hall). It can mean shared, for everyone, like English 'communal', but the municipal sense is the usual one.

room_name: La maison des associations · The clubs' hall
change: added (Monsieur Verbe mime, red beret; conjugation added); vocab room ST_existence_seg008 -> R_society_04
hook: "ah-day-RAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) JOINS the hiking club, and the club's big round sticker badge ADHERES so well that it stays stuck on his glove: ADHERE (sticker)
note: Adhérer means to join, to be a member (adhérer à un club, à un parti) and to stick, adhere (Le pneu adhère à la route). Adhérer à une idée is to support it. Un adhérent is a member; une adhésion is membership or adhesion.

room_name: L'exposition · The town exhibition
hook: "CRAYON (krwah-YAHN)": a smiling BELIEVER with a small cross on a chain colors a drawing of the village church with a giant CRAYON: CRAYON
note: Croyant means believing, religious (Il est très croyant = he is very religious); as a noun, un croyant, une croyante is a believer. Non croyant means non-believer. It comes from croire (to believe). Careful: crayon is French for pencil.

room_name: L'exposition · The town exhibition
hook: "fay-mee-NEEST": a grandma in a purple, white and green suffragette sash flexes her arm like a strongwoman, and her granddaughter proudly copies her: FEMINIST
note: Féministe means feminist (un mouvement féministe); as a noun, un or une féministe. Le féminisme is feminism. The word is the same for both genders. Féminin means feminine or women's (la mode féminine).

room_name: L'exposition · The town exhibition
hook: "mee-grah-TUHR": a V of MIGRATORY swallows swoops in through the open skylight, heading south, and a boy points up at them: MIGRATORY swallows
note: Migrateur means migratory (les oiseaux migrateurs). As a noun, un migrateur is a migratory bird. People who migrate are des migrants; la migration is migration, of birds or people.

room_name: L'exposition · The town exhibition
hook: "troh-pea-KAHL": in the TROPICAL corner, a man fans himself in the steamy heat beside a big potted banana palm: TROPICAL heat
note: Tropical means tropical (un climat tropical; les forêts tropicales). It can also mean scorching, sweltering (une chaleur tropicale; une nuit tropicale = a hot night above 20°C). Les tropiques are the tropics.

room_name: L'exposition · The town exhibition
hook: "ahn-troh-poh-loh-ZHEEK": an anthropologist studies an ancient clay pot through a magnifying glass, the class gathered around: ANTHROPOLOGY
note: Anthropologique means anthropological (une étude anthropologique). L'anthropologie is the study of human beings and their cultures; un anthropologue is an anthropologist. Anthropo- comes from Greek for human.

room_name: L'exposition · The town exhibition
hook: "ah-rees-toh-krah-TEEK": a snooty ARISTOCRAT in a powdered wig and lace cuffs peers down his nose through a lorgnette: ARISTOCRAT
note: Aristocratique means aristocratic, of the nobility, and also refined, distinguished (des manières aristocratiques). L'aristocratie is the aristocracy; un aristocrate (informally un aristo) is an aristocrat.

room_name: L'exposition · The town exhibition
hook: "fohn-DAY (FOUND-ed)": a man in medieval clothes lays the first stone, FOUNDING the village, a crowd in costume cheering: FOUNDED
note: Fondé means founded, established (une ville fondée au XIIe siècle) and, of an idea, well-founded, justified (une crainte fondée). Être fondé à faire = to be entitled to. Un fondé de pouvoir is a proxy or authorized agent.

room_name: L'exposition · The town exhibition
hook: "mahr-KSEEST": a student reads a thick red book under a marble bust of a big-bearded nineteenth-century thinker: MARXIST bust
note: Marxiste means Marxist, following Karl Marx's ideas (une analyse marxiste); as a noun, un or une marxiste. Le marxisme is Marxism. Do not confuse with Groucho Marx's films.

room_name: L'exposition · The town exhibition
hook: "noh-MAHD": a child peeks out of a round felt NOMAD tent, a yurt, that its family can fold up and move again and again: NOMAD yurt
note: Nomade means nomadic (un peuple nomade); as a noun, un or une nomade. It also means mobile, on the move (le travail nomade = remote, mobile work). The opposite is sédentaire (settled).

room_name: L'exposition · The town exhibition
hook: "ray-zee-dahn-SYEHL": a guide points at a big painting of a quiet RESIDENTIAL street of houses with gardens and swings: RESIDENTIAL street
note: Résidentiel means residential (un quartier résidentiel = a residential area, often with a hint of upscale). Une résidence is a residence or an apartment complex; une résidence secondaire is a vacation home.

room_name: Le buffet des délégations · The delegations' lunch
hook: "KORS (of COURSE)": a chef carries a CORSICAN chestnut cake shaped like a mountainous island, and a guest nods: of COURSE I'll have some!: CORSICAN (of COURSE)
note: Corse means Corsican, from Corsica (la cuisine corse); as a noun, un or une Corse is a Corsican and la Corse is the island. Le corse is the Corsican language. The word is the same in masculine and feminine.

room_name: Le buffet des délégations · The delegations' lunch
hook: "skahn-dee-NAHV": a SCANDINAVIAN guest happily assembles a flat-pack wooden chair with a little hex key: SCANDINAVIAN flat-pack
note: Scandinave means Scandinavian (le design scandinave); as a noun, un or une Scandinave. La Scandinavie is Scandinavia: Norway, Sweden and Denmark. Nordique (Nordic) also includes Finland and Iceland.

room_name: Le buffet des délégations · The delegations' lunch
hook: "ROO-MAN": a kangaroo (a ROO) hops up to a MAN and hands him a tray of ROMANIAN stuffed cabbage rolls from its pouch: ROO-MAN
note: Roumain means Romanian (la cuisine roumaine); as a noun, un Roumain, une Roumaine; le roumain is the Romanian language and la Roumanie is Romania. Careful: romain (no u) means Roman.

room_name: Le buffet des délégations · The delegations' lunch
hook: "kohn-tee-nahn-TAHL": a waiter carries a CONTINENTAL breakfast tray of croissants, jam and coffee: CONTINENTAL breakfast
note: Continental means continental, of a continent (le climat continental = hot summers and cold winters). In France, la France continentale is mainland France, as opposed to Corsica and the overseas territories. Le petit-déjeuner continental is a continental breakfast.

room_name: Le buffet des délégations · The delegations' lunch
hook: "mewl-tee-nah-syoh-NAHL": a busy MULTINATIONAL businesswoman wears five wristwatches up her arm, each set to a different country: MULTINATIONAL watches
note: Multinational means multinational (une entreprise multinationale); une multinationale is a multinational company. Multi- means many: multiculturel, multilingue.

room_name: Le buffet des délégations · The delegations' lunch
hook: "may-troh-poh-lee-TAN": a toy METRO train runs around the table on a little track, and a boy watches it go: METRO train
note: Métropolitain means metropolitan; in France it usually means mainland France (la France métropolitaine, as opposed to the overseas départements). Le métropolitain is the full name of the Paris subway, now le métro. Une métropole is a big city.

room_name: Le buffet des délégations · The delegations' lunch
hook: "kohns-tee-TWAHN": a girl lays out the CONSTITUENT parts of a sandwich side by side: bread, cheese, tomato and lettuce: CONSTITUENT parts
note: Constituant means constituent, making up a whole (les éléments constituants). L'Assemblée constituante was the body that wrote a constitution in 1789 and after. As a noun, un constituant is a component.

room_name: Le buffet des délégations · The delegations' lunch
hook: "teh-ree-toh-RYAHL": a TERRITORIAL goose spreads its wings and hisses at a guest who steps onto its patch of floor: TERRITORIAL goose
note: Territorial means territorial (les eaux territoriales; un animal territorial). In France, la fonction publique territoriale is local government service, and une collectivité territoriale is a local authority (region, département, commune).

room_name: Le buffet des délégations · The delegations' lunch
hook: "SWEES": guests dip bread into a bubbling pot of SWISS cheese fondue on long forks: SWISS fondue
note: Suisse means Swiss (le chocolat suisse); as a noun, un Suisse, une Suissesse or une Suisse; la Suisse is Switzerland. In France, un petit-suisse is a small fresh cheese for children. Manger en suisse means to eat alone without sharing.

room_name: Le buffet des délégations · The delegations' lunch
hook: "kay-bay-KWAH": a guest from QUEBEC pours golden maple syrup over a stack of pancakes, a red maple-leaf pin on her sweater: QUEBEC maple syrup
note: Québécois means from Quebec (la culture québécoise); as a noun, un Québécois, une Québécoise. Le québécois is also the French spoken in Quebec. The province is le Québec, the city is Québec (no article).

GENERAL rule: Centre-band rooms (adjectives/adverbs/verbs 384-896 px): generate a 1:1 square of the centre band and outpaint to 16:9; measure box centres after; drop a stray word rather than reroll the room.
GENERAL rule: Reject letterboxed outpaints; pad the square with flat gray on all four sides and ask to continue the same room's walls, floor and ceiling.
GENERAL rule: No microphone stand next to a figure whose hook is not about a microphone.
GENERAL rule: Only Monsieur Verbe wears white face paint; say 'no face paint' for criers, clowns and actors.
GENERAL rule: Next to a mime, name who holds each prop; the mime's hands stay empty unless the prop is his.
GENERAL rule: State the visible cue in the object (blur, fog, size) instead of relying on a facial expression.
GENERAL rule: For 'parts of' hooks write 'not stacked, each piece apart, side by side'.
GENERAL rule: Say human or animal for every body-part hook.
GENERAL rule: Put the room's central landmark on an adjective/adverb/verb so the centre band carries a hook.
GENERAL rule: Count the hook figures after every generation and every edit before measuring boxes.
GENERAL rule: Doors look the same color on both sides; when linking a new room, add its door to the existing room in the same pack.
GENERAL rule: Reserve a free full-height wall section for future doors in every new room.
GENERAL rule: When adding a door beside an existing door, edit from a version where both are clearly separate, change only color and glimpse, and name 'keep the strip of wall between'.
GENERAL rule: When a door edit removes furniture, mask the whole removed object or pick a wall with nothing in front of it.
GENERAL rule: Check name-plate width (long two-language names reach about 290-990 px) before placing a hotspot in the top band.
GENERAL rule: Respell syllables that read as pee/poo with 'pea' (troh-pea-KAHL) and override example sentences that mention smoking.
GENERAL rule: A door glimpse shows its destination room as planned and as painted: check the plan for where the door leads and name that room's walls, floor, seating and colors.
GENERAL rule: A door pair matches on both sides: same leaf count, color, style and open state; pass the other side's door as a reference.
GENERAL rule: Doors stand on the floor: frame, opening and threshold run down to the baseboard line; no floating doors.
GENERAL rule: A door edit removes everything in its way completely, and keeps every other door in the crop in its current state.
GENERAL rule: Glimpses show no digits, text, signs or people.
GENERAL rule: A dropped word's figure is painted out in the same pack (or the word gets a new hook and spot); no unexplained figures.
GENERAL rule: New figures stay clear of door leaves and openings; name the door and say it stays clear.
GENERAL rule: An edit mask on the frame edge runs to the edge; rects in a union mask overlap so no gap band is left.
GENERAL rule: Edits must not introduce artifacts: compare every pasted edit with its base at 2x and fix seams, dents and remnants before packing.
GENERAL rule: Record every crop box, mask, feather and sent prompt (including rejected tries) in the manifests as you go.
